current.headline: NASCAR won't race downtown in 2027; 2028 still in play
current.image_alt: NASCAR cars racing on Balbo Drive with the Chicago skyline behind
current.summary: NASCAR has announced it will not bring its Chicago Street Race back downtown in 2027, moving next year's event to Chicagoland Speedway in Joliet instead. The three-year run on a temporary course through Grant Park and nearby streets drew national attention but also road closures and weeks of setup and teardown that hit 34th Ward neighborhoods hard around the July 4th holiday. The 34th Ward office says it hopes to reach a 2028 agreement that makes financial sense for the city and holds the race on a weekend other than July 4th, while crediting NASCAR for faster setup and takedown and for keeping residents informed over the three years.

history.headline: Soul City Church's West Loop expansion divides the neighborhood
history.image_alt: Soul City Church at 1150 W. Adams St in the West Loop
history.summary: Soul City Church wants to build a four-story addition at 1150 W. Adams Street, including a 1,500-seat auditorium, children's classrooms, and community space, to fit a Sunday congregation of about 2,200. The plan needs a zoning change and has drawn pushback from neighbors who cite years of noise, bass, and parking complaints. The church says the new auditorium would use masonry walls and thick concrete to contain the sound.

history.headline: Ald. Bill Conway announces run for reelection in the 34th Ward
history.intro: Ald. Bill Conway will not run for mayor and will instead seek reelection to represent the 34th Ward. He released the following statement:
paragraphs: I'm proud to announce that I'm running for reelection as Alderman of the 34th Ward.
This morning I walked my three daughters to camp, saying hello to neighbors and snapping photos of issues to send to the 34th Ward team.
It reminded me why I love this job.
I have the incredible privilege of working every day to make our neighborhoods safer, stronger, and more prosperous.
Over several months, I've reflected on how I can best serve Chicago. After serious consideration, I've decided my place is here in the 34th Ward.
Chicago is at a critical juncture.
If we don't confront our financial challenges and debt with urgency and discipline, they'll eventually overwhelm every priority we care about: safer streets, good jobs, affordable housing, growth.
I'll continue to be an independent voice, supporting good ideas regardless of where they come from & speaking up when I believe we're on the wrong path.
I'm honored by the trust my neighbors have put in me. There's much more work to do & I'm excited for what's ahead.
